title: Power and Battery widget needs support for "multiple batteries for a single HID device"
line: Devices with several batteries, like earbuds with a case or split keyboards, now show each battery with its own number instead of the same name repeated.
explanation: Since UPower merged MR !337 (September 2026), each battery of a HID device with several batteries (Linux 7.1) reaches Plasma as its own UPower device, so the widget already lists all of them. But they all share the device's vendor and model, so the popup showed e.g. three identical "Sony WF-1000XM5" rows that couldn't be told apart. The battery model now appends "(Battery N)" when several batteries share a name, numbered in the natural order of their UPower paths (the kernel's battery report ids), and refreshes the names when batteries come and go.

commits.message:
components/batterycontrol: number batteries that share a device name

Devices like earbuds or split keyboards now show up with one battery per
part, but all of them got the same name, making them indistinguishable in
the Power and Battery widget. Each one now gets a "Battery N" suffix.

BUG: 518513

media.caption: A split keyboard (2 batteries) and earbuds (3 batteries): every battery shows the same device name
Each battery of the same device gets its own number
After one keyboard half disconnects, the remaining one goes back to the plain name

review.text: Now that UPower !337 exposes each battery, the remaining Plasma-side problem is telling them apart. Numbering batteries that share a name, with numeric-sorted UDIs and a refresh on add/remove, is a small and sensible fix that reuses the existing 'Battery N' wording. The fake-UPower media show both the before and after states and the fallback when one part disconnects. A nit for the MR: the dedup would sit more naturally inside BatteriesNamesMonitor. Calling updateBatteryName() on every other battery from data() also assigns 'Battery N' indexes to unnamed batteries in map order rather than display order, but they never collide, so this is cosmetic.
